'''Antonia Jane Jones''' (1943 – 2010) was a British mathematician and computer scientist. Her research considered number theory and computer science.

== Early life and education ==
Jones was born in 1943 in [[Queen Charlotte's and Chelsea Hospital]]. She was the first member of her family to attend university. Jones contracted polio as a child and lost both of her legs at the age of ten.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Antonia Jones Obituary (2011) - St. Augustine Record|url=https://www.legacy.com/amp/obituaries/staugustine/150288587|access-date=2021-01-31|website=www.legacy.com|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Buckley|first=Anne|date=1984-07-01|title=Women in Electrical Engineering Education|url=https://doi.org/10.1177/002072098402100302|journal=The International Journal of Electrical Engineering & Education|language=en|volume=21|issue=3|pages=197–212|doi=10.1177/002072098402100302|s2cid=111931564 |issn=0020-7209|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Jones attended the [[University of Reading]], where she studied mathematics and physics and graduated both with first class honours.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Antonia J Jones|url=http://users.cs.cf.ac.uk/O.F.Rana/Antonia.J.Jones/|access-date=2021-01-31|website=users.cs.cf.ac.uk}}</ref> She was a doctoral student in [[number theory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], where she completed her PhD in 1969. Jones joined the [[University of Nottingham]] after earning her doctorate, before joining [[Imperial College London]] as a Senior Lecturer. She spent a year at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], after which she joined the faculty at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-12-09|title=Antonia Jane Jones - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/antonia-jane-jones|access-date=2021-01-31|website=www.ias.edu|language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Jones returned to the [[United Kingdom]] in the 1970s, where she became a lecturer at [[Royal Holloway, University of London]]. Her interest switched from mathematics to computing and she began to explore acoustic pattern recognition.<ref name=":1" /> Whilst Jones struggled with the early computers, when technology became more accessible for people with physical disabilities she launched her own firm creating random access video controllers.<ref name=":1" />

In 1983 Jones joined [[Brunel University London]] at a lecturer in Information Technology.<ref name=":1" /> Jones later served as Professor of Evolutionary and Neural Computing at [[Cardiff University]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jones|first=Christopher|date=|title=Athena SWAN Bronze department award application|url =https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/845809/CardiffUniversityComputerScienceInformaticsAthenaSwanBronzeApplication.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016104357/https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/845809/CardiffUniversityComputerScienceInformaticsAthenaSwanBronzeApplication.pdf |archive-date=2019-10-16 |access-date=2021-01-31|website=Cardiff}}</ref> She exposed various security loopholes in banking infrastructure, including identifying significant potential fraud at [[HSBC]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2006-08-10|title=Security flaw leaves 3m HSBC online accounts open to fraud|url=http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2006/aug/10/news.accounts|access-date=2021-01-31|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Bobbie|date=2006-08-11|title=HSBC knew about security loophole in online banking|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2006/aug/11/news.money|access-date=2021-01-31|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Alongside her scientific research, Jones was involved with science communication and public engagement. She served as an electronic data consultant on the 1986 film ''[[Rocinante]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rocinante (1986)|url=https://www2.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/4ce2b79250a77|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321134258/http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/4ce2b79250a77|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 March 2017|access-date=2021-01-31|website=BFI|language=en}}</ref> She contributed to the 1998 [[British Science Association]] Festival of Science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=British Association for the Advancement of Science, 1998: Mathematical Sciences|url=http://www.maths.qmul.ac.uk/~rab/baas.html|access-date=2021-01-31|website=www.maths.qmul.ac.uk}}</ref> In 2007, Jones retired from Cardiff University.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Antonia Jones spent many years with her partner Barbara Quinn at their shared farmhouse in the Brecon Beacons. Upon her retirement in 2007, Jones moved to [[St. Augustine, Florida]].  Jones died on 23 December 2010. She is survived by Quinn and her sister Jenny Carrl.<ref name=":0" />
